Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

I checked twice because one shell was hidden under the cardboard flap. The butter dish has one stick, and there are two wrapped sticks in the freezer.

The main refrigerator shelf has a bowl of cooked lentils, dated Tuesday, and a covered plate with half a roasted squash. The lentils are for lunch tomorrow if they still smell fresh; that was my reminder, not a decision to serve them. There is a small container of grated Parmesan, about a third full, and a block of cheddar with one corner cut away. The cheddar is wrapped in wax paper, but one edge is exposed. Wrap that edge again after checking whether it has dried out. Leave it closed until someone can identify it; don’t guess from the shape of the container.

The utensil drawer has eight teaspoons, six dinner forks, and five table knives. One of the teaspoons is in the mug cupboard, probably left there after tea. The wooden spatulas are dry, and the small whisk is missing from its usual hook. I found it in the mixing bowl on the lower shelf. There are two clean cutting boards leaning beside the oven and one board on the counter that still needs washing. The roll of parchment paper has enough left for one small tray. Foil is nearly gone, but there is a spare roll in the utility cupboard. I wrote that down because I have looked for it in the kitchen three times this month.

The last reminders are for the shelves beside the sink. There are two new sponges under the sink, one bottle of dish soap in use, and a refill bottle that is still sealed. The cloths are clean and folded in the second drawer. The small jar of coarse salt is nearly full, while the box of kosher salt is down to about one cup. Peppercorns are in the grinder, with a little in the refill tin. Put the refill tin on the counter before making the soup, since I keep forgetting it is in the back of the cupboard. The pantry is less full than it looked from the doorway because two of the large tins are empty, and the bag of rice on the floor is only about a third full. I checked the labels as I went and wrote the open dates on the masking tape if the date was still readable. The list is for the back kitchen and the small prep room, not the upstairs cupboard.

Starting with dry goods, the shelf beside the mixer has four sealed bags of bread flour and one open bag with about two kilos left. There are six kilos of whole wheat flour in the tall tub, and the lid fits, but the hinge is cracked. I found three bags of cornmeal. One is open and should be used first. We have two unopened boxes of baking soda and a nearly full box of baking powder. The brown sugar tin is full, and the white sugar bin is a little under half. There are five kilos of basmati rice and one kilo of red lentils. The rolled oats are in two jars, with three cups in the smaller jar.

On the lower pantry shelf, I counted eleven cans of chickpeas, eight cans of diced tomatoes, and four cans of coconut milk. Two tomato cans have dents near the rim, but neither is leaking. The label on one can says best before October, and I could not find a year on it. The vegetable stock cartons are all unopened. There are seven in the case and two loose beside it. We have one jar of tahini with a quarter left and three sealed jars behind it. The oil is in the gray bin under the counter, and there are two full bottles of olive oil plus an open bottle that feels about one third full.

Section 1: Small prep room
1. One carton of eggs with nine left and a second carton with twelve.
2. Three blocks of salted butter and one block of unsalted butter. The unsalted one is wrapped in foil and has a Monday date written on it.
3. Two tubs of plain yogurt, both sealed, and one small tub of sour cream that was opened yesterday.
4. There are four lemons in the wire bowl and six limes in the drawer. The limes are firm, but two lemons have soft spots.
5. The herb containers are parsley, dill, and mint. Parsley is almost empty, and the dill lid is missing.
6. One loaf of sandwich bread is in the freezer with a date from last month. I could not tell whether it was put there on the second or the twelfth.

About the refrigerator door, I found three jars of mustard, one yellow mustard and two Dijon, and the small jar of mayonnaise is nearly empty. There are four jars of pickles, but one lid is sticky, so I set it on a plate instead of putting it back in the door. The shelf above the crisper has six cans of sparkling water and a bottle of apple juice that is open. The juice label says use within seven days, but nobody marked when it was opened. There are two containers of cooked beans in the back, and I don't know if they are from Tuesday or Wednesday, so I left them where they were rather than guess about the date.

The freezer inventory is harder because the drawer sticks when it is full. I counted two bags of peas, one bag of corn, and one bag of spinach. The spinach package has a small tear, but the food inside is still frozen. There are four portions of vegetable soup in round containers and two containers of tomato sauce with tape labels. One says basil, and the other says plain. Both labels have the same date, so maybe they were made together. The small basket has three unopened packs of yeast and a bag of walnuts with no label on it. I did not move the ice tray because it was frozen to the shelf, and I didn't want to break it.

In the dry storage cabinet, there are two rolls of parchment paper, one roll of foil, and four rolls of paper towels. We have one unopened box of sandwich bags and a partly used box of freezer bags. The cleaning shelf is separate, and I did not include those items in the food count. The red measuring cup is missing from the utensil jar, but the metal one cup measure is there. The digital scale turns on, though the display fades if it is left on for more than a minute. I found the spare batteries in the drawer by the sink and put them beside the scale, not inside it, because I wasn't sure whether they were new.

Can you check whether we should order another bag of bread flour and more lemons before Friday? I think the flour will last through the weekend if we use the whole wheat first, but I'm less certain about the lemons because two are already soft. Please tell me whether you want me to throw out the two questionable cans or keep them aside for you to inspect, and whether the open juice should be used today or discarded.
